tasks.short: Screen the literature, design the study and get ethics approval, collect data with participants, enter and analyse the data, and write up the findings.

steps.what: Occupational therapist screens literature to conduct research in occupational therapy

loop.input: Abstracts from a database search and the therapist's include or exclude labels so far.
loop.output: The abstracts reordered so the most likely relevant come first.
loop.check: The therapist reads and labels every abstract shown, so inclusion is the therapist's judgement; a stop rule fixed beforehand is tested on a set of known relevant studies, and screening goes on by hand when the test misses any of them.
loop.stop: Stops when the fixed number of irrelevant abstracts in a row is reached and all known relevant studies were found; otherwise the therapist screens on.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword filters either miss studies or return thousands of abstracts.

steps.what: Occupational therapist designs the study and applies for ethics approval
Occupational therapist collects data with participants
Occupational therapist enters and analyses the data in a spreadsheet
Occupational therapist writes up the findings

tasks.design: Literature screening uses active learning: the model reorders abstracts while the therapist labels them, with a stop rule fixed beforehand and tested on known relevant studies. Participant data are captured on electronic study forms ({DATA_PLATFORM}) with range checks, and the analysis set out in the protocol runs as a fixed script, so data are not typed into spreadsheets. Designing the study, collecting data and writing up stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Thousands of abstracts were screened one by one and data typed from paper forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Active learning screening tools and electronic study forms are available to researchers.
tasks.still_hard: Occupational therapy studies are small and recruitment is slow.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the question that matters for daily practice.
tasks.altitude: The therapist labels and interprets instead of screening and typing.

reach.learn: Whether screening and data are reproducible.

evidence.claim: Active learning screening tools reorder abstracts while a person labels them.
Health data are special category data; a solely automated decision needs an article 22(2) basis.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research question to findings written; publication is outside.
Input contract: database search exported; fallback is screening by hand.
Every included study is labelled by the therapist.

s1 keeps 50 because the ranking lets the therapist stop before reading every abstract. s4 keeps 40 for checking flagged values and reading the analysis; typing data and building tables go. Filling the electronic forms during data collection takes about the time paper took, so s3 keeps 100.
research_questions: How many abstracts are screened before the stop rule?

incremental.description: Occupational therapist sets up the study forms and analysis script for each study.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: narrow topics with few abstracts, so ranking saves little and s1 keeps 80, and the data need much cleaning, so s4 keeps 70 (8.0); high: broad reviews and clean electronic forms (18.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Visit the workplace and observe tasks, talk with the employee and employer, judge health risks, write the advice report, check it, and send it.

steps.what: Occupational therapist visits the workplace and observes tasks
Occupational therapist talks with the employee and employer about workload and transition to retirement
Occupational therapist judges health risks in the workplace and decides the advice
Occupational therapist writes the advice report
Occupational therapist checks the final report: findings and advice match the assessment, the employer's copy holds no medical data, and the recipients are right
Occupational therapist sends the checked report to the employee and employer: by e-mail today, by one release as a secure message after the change

tasks.design: The therapist fills a structured workplace assessment on a tablet during the visit, with standard risk items, measurements and photos, and the report template is filled from it, so findings are not copied from notes afterwards; the therapist still writes the advice. The therapist checks the report and releases it to the employee and employer as a secure message. Observing, talking and judging risks stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports were written from handwritten visit notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Tablet assessment forms feed report templates.
tasks.still_hard: Employers and employees want different things from the advice.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the adjustment that lets an older worker keep the job.

evidence.claim: Tablet assessment forms can feed report templates.
Health data are special category data under GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the advice request to the report sent; workplace changes are outside.
Input contract: assessment form agreed with the practice; fallback is handwritten notes.
The report to the employer holds no medical data.
Employees' and employers' time does not change.

Filling the assessment on a tablet during the visit takes about the time notes took, so s1 keeps 100. s4 keeps 75: findings and measurements fill from the assessment, but the advice is written by the therapist. s6 keeps 10 for the release.
research_questions: Do employers act on the advice more often?

incremental.description: Occupational therapist keeps the assessment form current.

approvals.approved_version: The advice report exactly as checked by the therapist in s5, sent once by secure message to the named employee and employer; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: complex workplaces need most of the report written, so s4 keeps 90 (5.5); high: standard workplaces where the assessment fills most findings (7.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Discuss work wishes and abilities with the patient, search for suitable vacancies, contact employers, coach the patient at work, and note progress.

steps.what: Occupational therapist discusses work wishes and abilities with the patient
Occupational therapist searches job sites to help patients locate jobs
Occupational therapist contacts employers about placements
Occupational therapist coaches the patient to hold the job
Occupational therapist notes progress in the record

tasks.design: Saved searches on job sites, filtered on hours, travel distance and physical demands from the patient's work profile, send new vacancies to the therapist, so they do not browse sites each week. Progress is noted in a short structured template in the record ({OTHER}); this first record keeps most of its time. Discussing work wishes, contacting employers and coaching stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job sites were browsed by hand for each patient.
tasks.enabler_now: Job sites offer saved searches with alerts.
tasks.human_edge: Persuading an employer to try a patient for two weeks.

evidence.claim: Job sites offer saved searches with alerts.

assumptions: Boundary: from the work goal to progress noted; employment contracts are outside.
Input contract: work profile kept by the therapist; fallback is browsing.
Contacting employers and coaching do not change.
s2 keeps 50 for reading the vacancies sent; browsing sites goes. s5 keeps 85 because the template only saves layout; the progress note is the therapist's own record.

incremental.description: Occupational therapist sets up saved searches per patient.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: saved searches miss many suitable vacancies, so the therapist still browses and s2 keeps 80 (4.2); high: saved searches as designed (10.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The occupational therapist keeps designing studies, judging workplace risks and coaching patients into work; abstract screening, typed data and job browsing shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A therapist with more time for patients and employers.
